newsitem.title: GERMANY: "Strong woman" Albright applauded after Bonn visit.
newsitem.headline: "Strong woman" Albright applauded after Bonn visit.

text.p: New U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright was a big hit on her visit to Bonn but her whirlwind global tour was something even travel-hungry Japanese tourists would not relish, newspapers said on Tuesday.

Albright, on her first overseas tour since taking office in January, was in Bonn on Sunday and Monday as part of an 11-day dash through Europe and Asia also taking in Rome, Paris, Brussels, London, Moscow, Seoul, Tokyo and Beijing.
"Nine capital cities in eleven days. Even Japanese tourists would not inflict that on themselves," said the Tagesspiegel daily in Berlin.
"The strong woman from Washington" was making so many stops to be sure she did not offend anyone, it said, and she certainly left a good impression in Bonn.
"This resolute woman is exactly to the taste of the Chancellor. Helmut Kohl was impressed with her on their first meeting," it wrote.
"A fresh breeze blew through Bonn," the popular Bild daily gushed. Albright's visit was "an impressive demonstration of the policy of plain speaking."
Bild said Albright had clearly and concisely laid down the U.S. position on one of the focal points of her trip -- NATO's planned eastward expansion.

The Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung said Albright was the opposite of her predecessor Warren Christopher. "He was quiet, discreet and ready to compromise -- she comes across as brusque, decisive and open."

The press approvingly highlighted Albright's blunt criticism of the Church of Scientology for charging Germany treated its members as the Nazis did the Jews. She called the comparison "historically inaccurate and distasteful."
The Czech-born secretary, who was brought up a Christian, only learned last month that three of her Jewish grandparents were killed by the Nazis in the Holocaust.

German newspapers have reported about her background but it has played no part in their assessment of her or her policies. "That's a big issue in the American press, but it's not one here," a U.S. diplomat said.
Albright travelled to Paris from Bonn on Monday afternoon and arrived in Brussels on Tuesday.
